transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Um, well, I came in because... honestly, I just feel so wound up almost all the time. It's like my whole body is just constantly bracing for the next bad thing to happen, you know? Like, I'll just be sitting at my desk—I do computer support, so I'm at my desk a lot, looking at screens, dealing with tickets and user issues, which can be stressful on its own, but this is different. It's like this physical tightness, this tension that just doesn't go away. Even when I log off and try to do something fun, like... I go to this dance night with some friends from grad school, and I love dancing, I really do, but lately, I can't even relax there. I'm on the dance floor, the music is playing, people are having a good time, and I'm just standing there with my shoulders up to my ears, feeling this buzzing, restless energy like I need to jump out of my skin. It's exhausting, honestly, just carrying all this tension around from the moment I wake up until I try to go to sleep, and it's starting to make everything feel so much harder than it needs to be.
Have you experienced any episodes where you felt an intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?

Um, like a sudden thing? No, I don't think so. It's not really like... a sudden wave that crashes over me, you know? I've heard about people having those moments where they suddenly feel like they can't breathe or they're going to pass out, but for me, it's not like a switch flips out of nowhere. It's more of a slow burn, I guess? Or like a hum in the background that just gets louder and louder over the course of the day. 

Like, I'll start my shift at 8 AM, and I'll already feel a little tight, and then by the time I've helped the fifth person reset their password or figure out why their VPN keeps dropping—which happens literally all the time with this new security update they pushed out last week, it's been an absolute nightmare for the support team to deal with—I'll just suddenly realize that my jaw is completely locked and my stomach is in knots. But it didn't happen in just a few minutes, it just sort of built up over hours of sitting there. It never really spikes into this intense, terrifying peak where I feel like I'm losing control right in that second. It's just always there, stretching out for hours and hours, dragging me down, rather than hitting me all at once. So, no, not that sudden intense peak you're talking about, just this endless, exhausting dread that never really shuts off.
Have you been avoiding any activities or situations because of these feelings of tension and dread?

Um, yeah, I have actually. I mean, it's getting to the point where it's really messing with my daily life, which is why I finally decided to make an appointment. Like with work, I usually pride myself on being really efficient, you know? I'm the person people come to when they have a weird issue that no one else can figure out. But lately, with this constant dread hanging over me, I just... I can't focus. I'll get a ticket, a simple one, like someone needing software installed, and I'll just stare at it, feeling this tightness in my chest, and I'll end up double-checking my steps three or four times. It's ridiculous, I know how to do it, I've done it a hundred times, but I just get so paralyzed by this feeling that I'm going to mess it up or that something terrible is going to happen if I don't do it perfectly. 

Because of that, I've started falling behind on my queue. It's embarrassing, honestly. My coworkers have had to start picking up the slack, and I can tell they're getting annoyed, even though they haven't said anything directly. I just feel so guilty about it, which only makes the tension worse, you know? 

And it's not just work, either. Like I mentioned those dance nights earlier? I've actually skipped the last three. I just couldn't bring myself to go. The thought of being in that crowded room, trying to pretend I'm having fun when I feel like a tightly coiled spring... it was just too much. I'd get dressed, look in the mirror, and just feel completely overwhelmed, so I'd text my friends some excuse about having a headache or being tired from work. I've also been skipping these mentoring sessions I do for undergrads in my old program. I usually love doing them, it's so rewarding, but right now, I just feel like I barely have the energy to keep myself together, let alone help someone else navigate their career. So yeah, I'm definitely avoiding things, and I hate it, because I feel like my life is just shrinking down to my desk and my couch, and even there, I can't relax.
Have you been experiencing any feelings of sadness or hopelessness lately?

Um... sadness? I mean, not really, no. It's not like I'm sitting around crying or feeling like there's no point to anything, you know? I'm not feeling down in that heavy, dark way that I think people mean when they talk about being depressed. It's really just the stress, the constant, never-ending stress. 

I guess I feel frustrated, definitely. Like, incredibly frustrated with myself for not being able to just snap out of it. Like I was saying about missing the dance nights and the mentoring—I'm not skipping them because I don't care anymore or because I feel hopeless about my life. I actually really want to go! I want to be out there, I want to be helping those undergrads, because I remember how lost I felt when I was in their shoes trying to figure out what to do with my degree. I want to be doing all those things, but I just feel too wired and on edge to actually do them. It's like my brain wants to participate in my life, but my body is stuck in this permanent "brace for impact" mode. 

So it's not sadness, exactly. Maybe a little bit of grief for the fact that I'm missing out on things I enjoy right now, but it's mostly just this exhausting, buzzing anxiety. I don't feel hopeless, I just feel... trapped by the tension, I guess? Like I'm waiting for the other shoe to drop all the time, and it's taking up all my energy. But no, I wouldn't say I feel sad or hopeless about the future, just really, really tired of feeling this wound up today.
Have you ever had a sudden episode where you felt intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes, even if it's not what's primarily bothering you now?

Wait, isn't that what we were just talking about a few minutes ago? Yeah, no, like I was saying before, it's really never a sudden peak for me. I've never had a moment where I'm just sitting there and BAM, out of nowhere I'm terrified and my heart is pounding out of my chest in the span of two minutes. It's just not how my brain works, I guess. 

I mean, even going all the way back to when I was in grad school, pulling all-nighters to finish my thesis, the stress was always this long, drawn-out marathon. Never a sprint. I'd sit in the library for twelve hours straight, and the dread would just slowly layer itself on top of me, like... like putting on heavier and heavier winter coats, if that makes sense? You don't really notice how heavy it is until you're completely weighed down and can barely move. And it's the exact same way now with my IT job. There's no sudden spike of intense fear where I feel like the world is ending right that second. It's just that constant, simmering tension that starts the moment my alarm goes off and I realize I have to face the ticket queue again. 

So, no, definitely never any sudden episodes like that, not in the past and not now. It's never a quick peak. It's always just that endless, exhausting background noise that I was telling you about.
Do you have any recurring thoughts or urges that you feel compelled to repeat over and over?

Um, recurring thoughts or urges? No, not really. I mean, I know I mentioned double-checking my steps when I'm working on a ticket, but it's not like I feel this overwhelming compulsion that I *have* to do it or else something specific will happen, you know? It's not like a ritual or anything like that. It's just that I'm so worried I'm going to mess up that I second-guess myself. 

Like, if I'm installing a new software package for someone in the marketing department—they always need these really specific design programs that have a million little configuration settings—I'll go through the installation, and then I'll just sit there and look at it, and my brain will just be spinning with, "Did I check the right box for the licensing server? Did I map the drive correctly? What if they try to open it tomorrow for a big presentation and it crashes and it's all my fault?" So I'll go back and look at the settings again. But it's not an urge, really, it's just the anxiety making me doubt my own competence. 

And it's definitely not like I have thoughts popping into my head that I'm trying to get rid of, or like I have to wash my hands a certain number of times or tap the desk before I can start working. Nothing like that. It's just the constant worry about the future, about messing up at work, about letting people down. Like, my brain is just constantly churning over all the possible ways things could go wrong, but it's not a specific thought that repeats like a broken record, if that makes sense? It's more of a general theme of impending doom, I guess you could call it. But yeah, no specific urges or anything like that. Just the usual, exhausting worry.
Is there a particular situation or thing that you feel is causing your anxiety, or does it feel more like a general feeling that's with you all the time regardless of what you're doing?

It's definitely not just one thing, no. I mean, it kind of started out feeling like it was just about the condo, you know? Like, when I first bought the place, I was so focused on the mortgage payments and whether the HOA fees were going to go up, and if the roof needed fixing... but it doesn't stay on the condo anymore. It just sort of morphed into this giant cloud that follows me everywhere. 

Like, it just jumps around all day. I'll be lying in bed, and instead of just worrying about the condo, suddenly I'm agonizing over a conversation I had with my cousin three days ago. Like, did I say something wrong? Is she upset with me because I had to cancel our coffee date? I'll spend an hour just dissecting that. And then, once I finally get out of bed and log into work, it immediately shifts to whether I'm going to make a mistake on a support call. I'll be helping someone reset their password, which I've done a thousand times, but my brain is just screaming, "What if you accidentally lock them out of the entire system and they lose all their work and you get fired?" 

And it doesn't even stop there! If I have a quiet moment, it just spirals out into these huge, existential things. Like, how am I ever going to save enough money for retirement? Or how am I ever going to move forward with my life if I'm stuck in this entry-level IT job forever? It's like my brain is just constantly scanning for the next thing to panic about, and it doesn't matter what I'm doing—whether I'm at work, or trying to relax, or just taking a shower—the worry is always there, just attaching itself to whatever is closest. So, yeah, it's definitely a general feeling that's just... always with me, all the time.
Have you been having trouble sleeping due to these feelings of anxiety?

Oh, God, yes. Sleep is... sleep is basically a joke at this point. It’s actually one of the worst parts of all this, because by the time the day is over, I am just physically and mentally drained. Like, I’ll crawl into bed at maybe 10:30 or 11:00, and my body is just begging for rest, but the second my head hits the pillow, it’s like someone flips a switch in my brain. 

Suddenly, it’s not quiet anymore. It’s just this loud, looping reel of everything I’m stressed about. I’ll start thinking about the condo again, and then I’m mentally reviewing the HOA notices we got last month, trying to remember if I paid that special assessment fee. And then it shifts to work, and I’m literally lying there in the dark, staring at the ceiling, replaying the IT tickets I closed that day. I’ll start wondering, did I actually verify that the backup ran before I wiped that user’s hard drive? What if I missed a step in the protocol? What if they log in tomorrow and all their files are gone? 

And it just goes on and on like that. I’ll look at the clock and it’s midnight, then it’s 1:00 AM, then it’s 2:00 or 3:00 in the morning, and I’m still wide awake, just vibrating with anxiety. I try all those things people suggest, you know? Like deep breathing or listening to white noise, but nothing shuts it off. And then, even when I finally do manage to fall asleep, it’s not real sleep. It’s so light and restless, and I’ll wake up at 6:30 when my alarm goes off feeling like I just closed my eyes five minutes ago. I never, ever wake up feeling rested. It’s just this constant cycle of exhaustion, and it makes dealing with everything else the next day so much harder because I’m just running on fumes.
Is your anxiety usually focused on a specific worry or concern, or is it more of a general feeling of apprehension about anything that could go wrong?

Yeah, like I was kind of saying a little bit ago, it’s definitely the latter. It's just... everything. It really doesn't stay on one specific concern at all. 

Like, I know I mentioned the condo earlier, and that was definitely the big trigger at first, but my worry absolutely doesn't stay on the condo anymore. It’s almost like my brain gets bored of one panic and has to find a fresh one? So it just jumps around all over the place. Like, it'll jump from that to whether my cousin is still upset with me. And I’ll literally sit there analyzing the last three text messages she sent me, looking at the punctuation, wondering if her using a period instead of an exclamation mark means she’s secretly furious and just not saying it. 

And then, before I can even resolve that in my head, I’m already onto the next thing, like whether I’m going to make a massive mistake on a support call. I'll start picturing the user yelling at me, or my manager calling me into an unexpected Zoom meeting to fire me because I accidentally deleted a VIP's email archive or something stupid like that. 

And from there... I don't know, it just spirals into this huge, heavy dread about my whole existence. Like, how am I ever going to save any actual money? Am I going to be stuck doing password resets and troubleshooting printer drivers until I'm sixty? How do people even move forward with their lives when everything feels so incredibly precarious? 

So, um, yeah. It’s definitely not just one specific thing. It’s like a web, you know? One little worry just connects to a dozen other worries, and it just spreads out over everything. It's just this constant, humming apprehension in the background of my life about literally anything that could possibly go wrong.
Do you often feel restless?

Yes, absolutely. I mean, honestly, that's a huge part of why I finally decided I needed to come in and talk to someone. I just feel so... wound up, almost all the time. It’s like my body is constantly bracing for the next bad thing to happen, you know? Like I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop, even when there's no logical reason for it. 

I'll just be sitting at my desk, doing something completely mindless, like responding to a routine email or checking a ticket status, and my shoulders will be practically up to my ears. My jaw is always clenched, and my stomach is in knots, and I just feel this... this buzzing energy, like I need to jump out of my skin or run away, but there's nowhere to run to. 

And it's not just at work, either. It ruins the things I actually like doing. Like, I go to this dance night sometimes—or I try to, anyway—and I love it, it's supposed to be fun and a way to let off steam. But even there, when I'm just trying to enjoy the music and move around, I can't relax. My muscles are just so tight, and I'm so tense, like I'm physically preparing for a disaster right in the middle of the dance floor. It's exhausting, honestly. It's like my nervous system is stuck in overdrive and I can't figure out how to turn it off. I just want to be able to sit on my couch and actually feel relaxed, but my body just won't let me. It's just this constant, physical tension that never really goes away.
Do you feel like your anxiety is related to a fear of having a panic attack?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I know what a panic attack is, or at least I've read about them, and I don't think I've ever actually had one. It's not like I'm sitting around terrified that my heart is going to suddenly start pounding out of my chest or that I won't be able to breathe, you know? It's not that sharp, sudden, overwhelming terror that comes out of nowhere. 

It's more like... well, like I was saying before, it's this constant, low-grade hum of worry. It's the tension in my shoulders and the racing thoughts at 2:00 AM. It's not a fear of a specific physical attack happening to me. It's just a fear of... everything else. The condo, the IT tickets, my cousin, my future... just all of it swirling together into this giant ball of dread that never really goes away. But no, not a fear of a panic attack itself. I don't think that's what's driving this at all. It's just the day-to-day stuff that feels so completely unmanageable.
Do you have any recurring, intrusive thoughts that you try to suppress or ignore?

No, not really. I mean, I definitely have thoughts that I don't *want* to be having, like the stuff about my cousin or worrying about messing up a support ticket, but I wouldn't call them intrusive in the way you're probably meaning. Like, it's not some sudden, weird, disturbing image flashing in my head that I'm desperately trying to push away. 

It's more just... my normal worries, just playing on a loop, you know? Like, I'll be trying to watch a show, and my brain will just be like, "Hey, remember that email you sent to the marketing director? What if you sounded too abrupt?" And I'll try to ignore it and focus on the TV, but it's not like I'm horrified by the thought itself. I'm just annoyed that my brain won't shut up about it. 

So I don't really have to suppress them, per se. I just try to distract myself, which usually doesn't work anyway because I'll just end up Googling "how to write professional emails" for an hour instead of watching the show. But yeah, no weird, intrusive, out-of-nowhere thoughts that I'm trying to block out. Just the regular, exhausting chorus of everyday anxieties that I can't seem to turn down the volume on.
Do you avoid certain situations because you're afraid of feeling overwhelmed or having a reaction similar to what you've described as your constant tension?

I don't think I avoid things, exactly. I mean, I still go to work, I still do my job, I still try to go to that dance night when I can drag myself there. It's not like I'm hiding in my apartment refusing to go outside or anything like that. I guess... well, actually, sometimes I might put off dealing with certain things, but it's not because I'm afraid of having some kind of huge reaction or breaking down in public. It's more just... I'm already so exhausted from being tense all the time that the idea of adding more stress on top of it just feels impossible. 

Like, if my cousin wants to meet up for coffee to talk about some drama she's having, I might make up an excuse and say I have to work late, just because I know listening to her is going to make my shoulders even tighter and my stomach even more tied in knots, and I just don't have the energy for it that day. Or if there's a really complicated IT ticket that I know is going to take hours to untangle and involve talking to three different departments, I might accidentally-on-purpose leave it at the bottom of my queue for a day or two, just to give myself a tiny bit of breathing room before I have to deal with the inevitable headache it's going to cause. 

But I wouldn't call it avoiding situations out of fear, really. It's more like... strategic procrastination, maybe? Just trying to manage my energy levels so I don't completely burn out. I don't know if that makes sense. But yeah, I don't stay away from places or events because I'm scared of feeling overwhelmed. I'm already overwhelmed, pretty much everywhere I go, so avoiding things wouldn't really fix the problem anyway, you know? It's just a matter of trying to get through the day without completely running out of steam.
Is there a particular theme or set of themes that your worries tend to center around?

Well, it used to be mostly about the condo, you know? Like, when I first moved in, I was so fixated on everything that could go wrong with it—the plumbing, the HOA fees, the neighbors, just the whole concept of owning property and being responsible for it. But now... it's like my worry doesn't stay on the condo anymore. It just sort of... jumps around. 

It's like this moving target. One minute I'm obsessing over whether my cousin is upset with me because I took too long to text her back, and I'll spend an hour analyzing the punctuation in her last message to see if she's mad. And then, before I even resolve that in my head, my brain is already moving on to work. I'll start agonizing over whether I'm going to make a mistake on a support call, like what if I give the wrong advice and completely crash someone's system? Even though I've done this job for years and I know what I'm doing, I just get this overwhelming dread that today is the day I'm going to mess it all up and get fired. 

And then, if I manage to talk myself down from that, it shifts to these big, existential things. Like, how am I ever going to save enough money? How am I supposed to move forward with my life when I feel stuck in this endless loop of IT tickets and paying bills? It's just... it's everything. It's my relationships, my job, my finances, my future. It's like my brain has this quota of worry it has to meet every day, and if one thing gets resolved, it just immediately latches onto something else to fill the space. So, yeah, I wouldn't say there's one specific theme. It's more like a rotating cast of themes, and they all just take turns keeping me up at night.
Is your anxiety present across most areas of your life, including work, relationships, and daily activities?

Yeah, definitely. It's... it's really everywhere. Like I was just saying, it's not just one thing anymore. I mean, it used to be so focused on the condo, just all the details of owning a place, you know? But now, it's like it has infected every single part of my day. 

It just jumps from one thing to the next. Like, I'll be sitting there, and suddenly I'm worrying about my cousin, like, "Is she upset with me? Did I say something wrong the last time we talked?" And I'll spend so much time just analyzing our last conversation, trying to figure out if there was some hidden meaning in her tone or her texts. 

And then, almost immediately, it shifts to work. I'll be taking a support call, something I've done a million times, and my brain will just start screaming, "What if you make a mistake? What if you give them the wrong fix and completely crash their entire system? What if this is the mistake that gets you fired?" And I'm just sitting there, trying to sound professional on the phone, while internally I'm just completely spiraling about losing my job. 

And it doesn't stop there, either. Then it moves on to the bigger picture stuff, like my finances and my future. I'll just be lying in bed, trying to sleep, and I'll start thinking, "How am I ever going to save enough money? How am I supposed to move forward with my life? Am I just going to be stuck in this same spot forever, just paying bills and fixing computers and worrying all the time?" 

So, yeah, it's work, it's my relationships, it's my daily life, it's my future... it's just this constant, exhausting cycle that touches pretty much everything I do. It really doesn't leave any area alone.
Is there any situation or activity where you feel completely free from anxiety?

Completely free? Um... wow. Honestly, no. I really can't think of a single time or place where my brain just... turns off. I mean, I wish there was. I really, really do. Sometimes I'll try to manufacture a situation like that, you know? I'll run a hot bath, or I'll sit down on the couch and put on a sitcom I've seen a hundred times, hoping that just the familiarity of it will let me zone out for a minute. 

But it never actually works. Because, well, like I was just saying a minute ago, the worry doesn't stay on the condo anymore. If it was just the condo, maybe I could just leave the building, go to a park, and feel completely fine! But it doesn't work like that. It just jumps. It constantly jumps from whether my cousin is secretly upset with me, to whether I'm going to make a huge mistake on a support call tomorrow and ruin someone's computer, to... to just how I'll ever save money or move forward with my life. 

It's like my brain has this endless Rolodex of things to stress about, and even if I'm doing something that *should* be relaxing, it's just spinning that wheel in the background, looking for the next thing to latch onto. So even if I'm physically in a calm situation, mentally, I'm completely tangled up in all of it. I just never get a break from it. It's always there, just waiting to switch to the next topic. So, yeah, no... there's nowhere I really feel free from it.
Is there anything that you do where your anxiety doesn't interfere at all?

Um... no. No, it really interferes with everything. I mean, I wish there was something I could do without it getting in the way, but it just bleeds into all of it. Like at work... I used to be so fast at clearing out my queue, you know? But lately, I've started falling behind on my support tickets. Because I'll get a ticket, and it'll be something so simple, something I've fixed a thousand times, like resetting a password or reconfiguring an email client, and I just... I can't just do it and move on anymore. I have to double-check every single step. And then triple-check it. Because my brain is telling me, "What if you clicked the wrong box? What if you accidentally deleted their entire inbox?" 

And it takes me so long to get through one ticket that my coworkers have actually had to start picking up the slack, which just makes me feel incredibly guilty and worried that they're all talking about how incompetent I am. And my supervisor even asked me the other day if my workload was too heavy, and I didn't even know what to say because it's not the workload, it's just my brain making everything take ten times longer than it should.

And it's not just work, either. It ruins the things I actually *like* doing. Like, I used to go to this dance night with my friends every other week, and I've skipped the last several of them. I'll get ready, and I'll be sitting on my bed, and I just feel so completely overwhelmed by everything—the noise, the people, worrying about if I'm acting weird or if my cousin is mad at me—that I just text them and say I have a migraine. And I also do this mentoring program for high school girls interested in tech, which I usually love, but I've skipped a few of those sessions lately too. I just feel like I can't show up and be this positive, encouraging role model when I'm constantly on the verge of a panic attack about my own life. So, yeah, it really just... it touches everything. There's nothing it doesn't mess up.
Is your anxiety affecting your personal relationships in the same way it affects your work or daily activities?

Yeah, I mean, like I was just saying a second ago, it really is... it's exactly the same kind of interference across the board. It all just bleeds together. Like, with my friends and those dance nights I mentioned? Skipping those isn't just about missing out on the music or the activity, it's... it's actively hurting my friendships. I'm isolating myself because I'm just too overwhelmed by all the noise in my head to even show up. I'll literally be sitting on my bed, fully dressed, makeup done, and I just can't bring myself to go out and face them. And then I sit there feeling like a terrible friend, wondering if they're mad at me for flaking again. 

And it's the same with the mentoring sessions with those high school girls. That's a relationship too, you know? They look up to me, and we've built this bond, but I've skipped several of those sessions lately because I just feel like a complete fraud. How am I supposed to sit there and give them life and career advice when I can barely get through my own day without spiraling? 

And it mirrors exactly what's happening at work, which I know I just rambled about, but... falling behind on my support tickets because I have to double-check and triple-check every little simple task, like a basic password reset... it doesn't just affect my stats, it affects my relationships with my team. My coworkers are having to pick up my slack now, and that's straining my relationship with them. I just sit at my desk worrying that they resent me, or that they're talking behind my back about how useless I've become. 

So, yes, the way it makes me freeze up and avoid things, or overthink every tiny detail... it's damaging my personal life and my friendships just as much as it's ruining my productivity at work. It's the exact same feeling of just... letting absolutely everyone down, all the time, because I'm too tangled up in my own head to function normally.
Is there anything that triggers your anxiety or is it always present regardless of the situation?

Well, it's... it's pretty much always there. Like I was saying, there's no situation where I feel completely free from it, so it's not like I need a specific trigger for it to start. It's more like a constant hum in the background of my life. I actually came in to see you because I feel wound up almost all the time. It's this physical sensation, you know? Like my entire body is just bracing for the next bad thing to happen. 

Even when I'm just sitting at my desk at work, doing something completely mundane, my shoulders are practically up by my ears and my jaw is clenched so tight it aches by the end of the day. And it's not just at work, it's when I'm trying to do fun things, too. Like when I used to actually make it to dance night with my friends before I started skipping them... I'd be there, the music would be playing, everyone's having a good time, and I'm just standing there feeling this incredible tension, like a coiled spring just waiting to snap. 

It's exhausting, honestly. Feeling like you're constantly on high alert, even when there's absolutely no threat around. I'll be sitting on my couch, trying to watch a sitcom, and my body still feels like I'm about to step out into traffic. So, no, I don't really need a trigger. The tension is just... it's my default state now. It's like my nervous system is stuck in the "on" position and I can't figure out how to flip the switch back.

What if you accidentally deleted their entire inbox?" 

And it takes me so long to get through one ticket that my coworkers have actually had to start picking up the slack, which just makes me feel incredibly guilty and worried that they're all talking about how incompetent I am. And my supervisor even asked me the other day if my workload was too heavy, and I didn't even know what to say because it's not the workload, it's just my brain making everything take ten times longer than it should.

And it's not just work, either. It ruins the things I actually *like* doing. Like, I used to go to this dance night with my friends every other week, and I've skipped the last several of them. I'll get ready, and I'll be sitting on my bed, and I just feel so completely overwhelmed by everything—the noise, the people, worrying about if I'm acting weird or if my cousin is mad at me—that I just text them and say I have a migraine. And I also do this mentoring program for high school girls interested in tech, which I usually love, but I've skipped a few of those sessions lately too. I just feel like I can't show up and be this positive, encouraging role model when I'm constantly on the verge of a panic attack about my own life. So, yeah, it really just... it touches everything. There's nothing it doesn't mess up.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's anxiety is generalized across different aspects of life
doctor.question: Is your anxiety affecting your personal relationships in the same way it affects your work or daily activities?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I've started falling behind on support tickets and double-checking simple tasks so much that coworkers have had to pick up the slack, and I've skipped several dance nights and mentoring sessions because I feel too overwhelmed to show up.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the impact of anxiety on personal relationships, work, and daily activities, which relates directly to functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I mean, like I was just saying a second ago, it really is... it's exactly the same kind of interference across the board. It all just bleeds together. Like, with my friends and those dance nights I mentioned? Skipping those isn't just about missing out on the music or the activity, it's... it's actively hurting my friendships. I'm isolating myself because I'm just too overwhelmed by all the noise in my head to even show up. I'll literally be sitting on my bed, fully dressed, makeup done, and I just can't bring myself to go out and face them. And then I sit there feeling like a terrible friend, wondering if they're mad at me for flaking again. 

And it's the same with the mentoring sessions with those high school girls. That's a relationship too, you know? They look up to me, and we've built this bond, but I've skipped several of those sessions lately because I just feel like a complete fraud. How am I supposed to sit there and give them life and career advice when I can barely get through my own day without spiraling? 

And it mirrors exactly what's happening at work, which I know I just rambled about, but... falling behind on my support tickets because I have to double-check and triple-check every little simple task, like a basic password reset... it doesn't just affect my stats, it affects my relationships with my team. My coworkers are having to pick up my slack now, and that's straining my relationship with them. I just sit at my desk worrying that they resent me, or that they're talking behind my back about how useless I've become. 

So, yes, the way it makes me freeze up and avoid things, or overthink every tiny detail... it's damaging my personal life and my friendships just as much as it's ruining my productivity at work. It's the exact same feeling of just... letting absolutely everyone down, all the time, because I'm too tangled up in my own head to function normally.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's anxiety is generalized or specific to certain situations
doctor.question: Is there anything that triggers your anxiety or is it always present regardless of the situation?

target_item.name: Restlessness_Tension
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I feel wound up almost all the time, like my body is bracing for the next bad thing even when I'm just sitting at my desk or trying to enjoy dance night.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the anxiety is triggered by specific things or always present. S058 describes feeling wound up almost all the time, regardless of the situation (e.g., sitting at desk, dance night).

patient.answer:
Well, it's... it's pretty much always there. Like I was saying, there's no situation where I feel completely free from it, so it's not like I need a specific trigger for it to start. It's more like a constant hum in the background of my life. I actually came in to see you because I feel wound up almost all the time. It's this physical sensation, you know? Like my entire body is just bracing for the next bad thing to happen. 

Even when I'm just sitting at my desk at work, doing something completely mundane, my shoulders are practically up by my ears and my jaw is clenched so tight it aches by the end of the day. And it's not just at work, it's when I'm trying to do fun things, too. Like when I used to actually make it to dance night with my friends before I started skipping them... I'd be there, the music would be playing, everyone's having a good time, and I'm just standing there feeling this incredible tension, like a coiled spring just waiting to snap. 

It's exhausting, honestly. Feeling like you're constantly on high alert, even when there's absolutely no threat around. I'll be sitting on my couch, trying to watch a sitcom, and my body still feels like I'm about to step out into traffic. So, no, I don't really need a trigger. The tension is just... it's my default state now. It's like my nervous system is stuck in the "on" position and I can't figure out how to flip the switch back.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of persistent and pervasive worry about everyday things, difficulty controlling worry, restlessness, feeling on edge, and sleep disturbance are consistent with Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD). The absence of sudden intense fear or discomfort that reaches a peak within minutes, which is characteristic of Panic Disorder, supports this diagnosis.
